title: Final closure audit

recoveryAuthorization.verdict: Recovery may PROPOSE. It may never authorize or dispatch. Verified in current source, not from a report.

m9Equivalence.mechanism: M9 replaces the guard with `if (true)`, so the body still assigns BOTH `action = healingResult.recoveredAction` AND `validation = healedVal`. Because `healedVal.allowed` is false, the very next gate at line 1248 (`if (!validation.allowed)`) takes the refusal path. The adoption M9 performs is therefore immediately discarded.
m9Equivalence.whyM9bIsCaughtInstead: M9b's anchor additionally includes the two assignment lines and neutralises `validation`, so the line 1248 gate is bypassed and the wrongly-typed healed target is actually dispatched.
m9Equivalence.conclusion: Genuine equivalence, and STRUCTURAL rather than accidental: a single variable (`validation`) is set by both the normal and the healed path and is what line 1248 consults. D-02 did not widen the escape surface.

privacyRecoveryInteraction.concern: recoverStaleTarget copies a `type` action's `text` verbatim into the healed action, so a raw value could in principle be laundered into a new action.
privacyRecoveryInteraction.measured: M5 re-validates the healed action and STILL refuses it on the same raw text; the healed `reason` is regenerated and never copied from the model; end to end through the loop nothing is dispatched.
privacyRecoveryInteraction.verdict: Closed. Recovery cannot launder a raw value past M5.

goalsExercised: Send money to a saved payee

mutations.note: The full 15 were re-run during the D-02 remediation against byte-identical code; the working tree was confirmed to match ed9d35e for every code path before this audit, and M9/M9b were re-run again during closure.

testCounts.note: 118 files / 1560 tests. Up from the 17.8 baseline of 116 / 1531 by exactly the two new remediation files (+1 D-01 with 16 tests, +1 D-02 with 13 tests). Nothing removed, no assertion weakened.

realChrome.infrastructure: Existing probes only. scratch/d02_real_chrome.ts reuses scratch/phase16_cdp.mjs. No new browser harness was built.
realChrome.whatIsStubbed: The model provider only. Real Chromium, production-built MV3 extension, real content-script perception, real egress path, real dispatch into the live page.

knownLimitationsCarriedForward.item: state.steps[].action retains a refused action's raw value in in-memory task state
knownLimitationsCarriedForward.why: Never dispatched, traced, sent to the provider or rendered. Documented and pinned by a test. Out of 17.9 scope.

knownLimitationsCarriedForward.item: Goal alignment is two hard-coded branches (transaction/history -> 0.90, account/details -> 0.88)
knownLimitationsCarriedForward.why: The fix made the branch reachable, not general. Widening the vocabulary is a design question, deliberately not taken.
Equivalence is structural (a single `validation` variable gates both paths) and was re-derived in this audit. Not a coverage gap.

notProven: Real-reasoner multi-step SUCCESS through the product path
Behaviour under a real provider outage or rate limit
repositoryHygiene: docs/evidence/phase17/17.8-benchmark/benchmark_results.json is rewritten by running the benchmark; timings differ each run while every substantive field is identical.
The two real-Chrome probes rewrite their committed evidence files with volatile Chrome tab IDs; the verdicts and check counts are identical.
scratch/ has no .gitignore rule, so harness journals and results are untracked noise that must be excluded by hand each time.
The 17.8 report's D-02 section described the defect as open; a forward reference to the 17.9 resolution has been added so a reader is not misled.
